record.paper_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
record.original_question: Let D1 , D2 be domains in {|z| < R}, and let λ1 (z) |dz| and λ2 (z) |dz| be their hyperbolic metrics. What is the least number A = A(R) such that the hyperbolic metric λ(z) |dz| of D1 ∩ D2 satisfies the inequality λ(z) < A(λ1 (z) + λ2 (z))? (W. H. J. Fuchs)

evidence.quote: Let D1 , D2 be domains in {|z| < R}, and let λ1 (z) |dz| and λ2 (z) |dz| be their hyperbolic metrics.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For $R>0$, let $\mathbb{D}_R = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| < R\}$. A domain $D \subset \mathbb{C}$ is called hyperbolic if $\mathbb{C} \setminus D$ contains at least two points; in this case $D$ carries a unique complete conformal metric $\lambda_D(z)\,|dz|$ of constant Gaussian curvature $-1$, called its hyperbolic metric (equivalently, $\lambda_D$ is determined by pulling back the Poincaré metric $|dw|/(1-|w|^2)$ through any holomorphic universal covering $\mathbb{D}\to D$, up to the standard normalization).

Let $D_1, D_2$ be hyperbolic domains contained in $\mathbb{D}_R$ such that $D_1 \cap D_2$ is nonempty and hyperbolic, and let $\lambda_1(z)\,|dz|$, $\lambda_2(z)\,|dz|$, and $\lambda(z)\,|dz|$ denote the hyperbolic metrics of $D_1$, $D_2$, and $D_1 \cap D_2$, respectively.

Determine the smallest constant $A = A(R)$, depending only on $R$, such that
$$\lambda(z) \le A\bigl(\lambda_1(z) + \lambda_2(z)\bigr)$$
holds for every $z \in D_1 \cap D_2$ and for every admissible choice of $D_1, D_2 \subset \mathbb{D}_R$.
artifact.status_search_result: A 2026 preprint addresses Fuchs's additive intersection problem for the hyperbolic metric. It shows that the supremum of $\lambda_{D_1\cap D_2}(z)/(\lambda_{D_1}(z)+\lambda_{D_2}(z))$ over all hyperbolic domains is $+\infty$, while if $D_1, D_2$ are restricted to be simply connected the sharp upper bound is $1$ (via Murai's subadditivity). The infimum of the ratio is $1/2$, attained iff $D_1=D_2$. Thus the question of the least constant $A(R)$ valid for arbitrary hyperbolic domains in $\mathbb{D}_R$ is essentially resolved (no finite universal $A$ exists), with sharp constants known under the simply-connected restriction.

status_evidence.title: On Fuchs's additive intersection problem for the hyperbolic metric
status_evidence.snippet: The supremum of λ_{D₁∩D₂}(z)/(λ_{D₁}(z)+λ_{D₂}(z)) is +∞ over all hyperbolic domains, and equals 1 when D₁,D₂ are simply connected; the infimum is 1/2, attained iff D₁=D₂.
status_evidence.claim: The Fuchs intersection problem has been recently analyzed, with sharp extremal constants determined.
